page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-4xCPU-24GB is a Cloud Native family virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor with a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The configuration includes 4 vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with 1.0 thread per core under a shared CPU allocation model. It is equipped with 24.0 GB of system memory, yielding 6.0 GB per core, and lacks local storage or dedicated GPU hardware. One complimentary public IPv4 address is included.

Benchmark results indicate a performance profile constrained by the shared CPU allocation. Single-core CPU performance via stress-ng is in the bottom 10% at 780.79, and multi-core performance falls in the bottom 25% at 3123.05. Geekbench testing shows an average single-core score of 1200.0 but a weak multi-core score of 3876.0. Memory performance is mixed, with average read-only small block bandwidth at 411.67 GB/sec, but weak large-block read bandwidth at 36.0 GB/sec. Database operations and Redis SET performance are also positioned in the bottom 25% of tested hardware.

Given the shared CPU allocation and lack of local storage, this server offers a budget-friendly entry point for workloads requiring moderate memory capacity but low CPU intensity. It is suitable for basic web serving, light text processing, and small-scale application hosting where continuous high CPU utilization is not required. It is less suitable for database hosting, heavy software compilation, or large language model inference due to weak multi-core and storage-related benchmark outcomes.
